title: refactor(sdk): defer request defaults to Gen
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Stops the SDK from injecting image, text, chat, audio, and transcription model defaults or the TTS voice default.
- Makes `/video/{prompt}` own its `veo` default and gives it a matching request schema.
- Makes `/v1/images/edits` own its documented `flux` default, preserving existing SDK behavior.
- Adds SDK serialization coverage and Gen permission tests for endpoint-specific defaults.

Tests: SDK suite (33 tests), SDK typecheck/build, Gen typecheck, and direct image/video schema checks.

gist.headline: Defaults moved into the hive
gist.blurb: The SDK has stopped guessing which model to bring. Gen now keeps each endpoint's defaults in one well-labeled garden bed.
gist.summary: The SDK now sends image, text, chat, audio, transcription, and TTS requests without injecting defaults, while Gen owns endpoint-specific defaults including `veo` for `/video/{prompt}` and `flux` for `/v1/images/edits`.
gist.impact: SDK users keep the existing documented video and image-edit behavior while API defaults can now be updated centrally by Gen instead of being duplicated in client code.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared defaults garden: Polli carefully carries a basket of model-name seeds from a small SDK tool shed to a central Gen greenhouse, where separate labeled beds for video and image edits grow `veo` and `flux` flowers. A helpful CRT monitor robot checks matching request-schema notes while code-vines connect the garden beds, representing defaults being owned centrally rather than copied into the SDK.
